## What's new in 1.43 STUDIO ROOM

- STUDIO ROOM: a new short, fully wet room preset based on Shield-77's own LIBRE settings (0.30 s, natural tone, zero pre-delay, 100% mix), confirmed by the creator's listening test. Bass and EQ remain independent.
- Faster bass-reactive SHAKE: up to 60 updates per second, shorter FFT window and improved transient detection.
- The visualizer listens to the final processed audio, including EQ, bass shaping, quality reduction, remix, reverb, compression and volume.
- Larger, slower VINYL display with an expandable deck.
- Adaptive ROCK STUDIO and independent LIBRE reverb controls remain available.

[Latest version details and test notes](#143-studio-room)

## About

SHIELD DJ Lite Web is a free personal project by Shield-77, made to share local music playback and creative audio effects with other users. It adapts the concepts of the original 3DS projects to native browser audio APIs, rather than emulating a console or porting its binary. Designed primarily for the **ASUS Chromebook CM14 (CM1406 series / CM1406CM4A, MediaTek Kompanio 540, 8 GB RAM, Mali-G57)**, it also targets recent Chromium-based desktop browsers.

Shield-77 chooses the features, creative direction and interface, and tests the player on their own physical Chromebook. ChatGPT assists with Web code, debugging, documentation and automated tests; Codex assisted development of the original 3DS projects. No AI service is required to run the player.

## Download and start

1. Download the [repository ZIP](https://github.com/Shield-77/Shield-DJ-Lite-Web/archive/refs/heads/main.zip) and extract it, or open the [HTML file page](https://github.com/Shield-77/Shield-DJ-Lite-Web/blob/main/index.html) and choose **Download raw file**.
2. Open `index.html` in Chrome. Check the version in the header to avoid using an older downloaded copy.
3. Choose a folder with **OUVRIR DOSSIER** or select individual files with **FICHIERS**. Press **LECTURE** after checking the system audio output.

No installer, account, subscription, server, developer mode or administrator access is required. Playback works offline. The HTML includes its full GPLv3 license. No music is supplied.

## Audio studio

| Feature | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Pitch and speed | Linked, 0.250x–2.000x, 0.001x slider resolution; buttons and arrows advance by 0.025x. The display reads the actual browser playback rate. |
| Quality | ORIGINAL bypass or 1–20 kHz in 1 kHz steps, Q16/PCM16 resampling adapted from Shield Theme Maker. Independent of pitch and glitch. |
| EQ | ROCK STUDIO (adaptive), POP STUDIO, POP ROCK STUDIO, AUTO STUDIO, Jazz, Clair, Extérieur, Classique; seven native filter nodes reused. |
| BASS STUDIO | PUNCH, DEEP BASS, ROCK DRIVE, DEEP + PUNCH; separate low, impact and corrective bands. |
| Reverb | Stereo synthesized convolution, STUDIO ROOM, CONCERT, CONCERT LIVE, CATHEDRALE, EXTRA and LIBRE. LIBRE has independent mix (0–100%), duration (0.30–5.00 s), tone and pre-delay (0–100 ms). LONG remains available for fixed presets. |
| Glitch Lab | Adaptive Glitch, Tape Wobble, Ghost Echo, Robot, Reverse Grains, Buffer Shatter; adjustable intensity. |
| Audio focus | Experimental VOICE ONLY and INSTRUMENT ONLY, based on stereo and frequency filtering, not AI source separation. |

CONCERT LIVE is inspired by measurements of a privately supplied concert recording. It is a synthetic room response, not a measured reconstruction of the venue. No recording is included. Smooth parameter transitions and output dynamics protection are retained; they are not a guarantee against clipping in every combination of effects.

## Visual Studio

| Mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| SPECTRUM | Transparent 40-band frequency spectrum over the local album artwork; up to approximately 30 fps. |
| SHAKE | Bass-transient-driven zoom and damped movement, up to 18% expansion and 60 visual updates per second. It reacts to low-frequency attacks, not isolated drum stems. |
| VINYL | Rotating record with album artwork, 10 rpm at normal playback speed, linked to pitch. Use AGRANDIR to expand the deck; REDUIRE or Escape to restore it. |
| STATIC | Still artwork, with animation and visual analysis disabled. |

Artwork is extracted locally from supported MP3, FLAC, Ogg Vorbis and Opus metadata, or from imported JPEG, PNG and WebP files with the same track filename (without extension), or named cover, folder, front or album in the same folder. If artwork is unavailable or unsupported, the supplied SHIELD DJ Lite logo is used automatically. Embedded M4A artwork is not yet supported. No online cover lookup is used.

Visual analysis is a read-only branch after the audio effects and output gain. Motion stops when playback pauses, the tab is hidden or reduced motion is requested. VINYL needs no audio analyser. Actual audio-to-screen timing depends on the device and browser.

## Library and controls

- Local MP3 and OGG Vorbis playback; WAV, FLAC and other supported formats depend on the browser.
- Recursive folder import, drag-and-drop, continuous virtual list, current-track locator and fullscreen.
- Accent- and case-insensitive search, partial words, arbitrary word order and limited typo tolerance.
- Modification-date sorting, alphabetical sorting and shuffle without repeats within a cycle; search and sorting do not change playback order.
- Unreadable files are skipped; playback stops when no usable files remain. No automatic playback on folder import.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Space | Play / pause |
| U / O | Previous / next |
| Left / Right | Pitch -/+ 0.025x (Shift uses the same step) |
| Up / Down | Audio quality |
| G / H | Adaptive Glitch / Buffer Shatter toggle |
| S / X / B | Shuffle / repeat / stop |
| F | Fullscreen |

The pitch reset restores exactly 1.000x. Holding a pitch arrow repeats after 350 ms, every 110 ms. The slider intentionally allows larger jumps. The desktop uses the original compact three-panel layout with independent library scrolling.

## v1.33: engine refinement

- Cache up to three sorted library index arrays; invalidate on folder import. Search no longer sorts the matching tracks again.
- Reflect only the changed control instead of rebuilding all UI state on each slider event.
- Hoist invariant remix calculations outside the sample loop; avoid repeated reset calls on empty worklet input.
- Flush pending settings on page hide.
- Keep the v1.32 CSS exactly; preserve the EQ curves, bass profiles, reverb impulse algorithms and exact pitch grid.

**Validation for v1.33:** 63 synthetic comparisons with v1.32 at 44.1/48/96 kHz, with 23,700,600 identical stereo-channel samples across different block sizes; 15 search/sort cases over 5,000 synthetic tracks; 63 DSP regression scenarios and 15 standalone resampling tests executed in a JavaScript environment. No physical Chromebook CPU measurement or listening test was performed for this version. The browser test script was updated for the current pitch and independent glitch/quality behavior, but has not been rerun for v1.33.

See [development history and prior test notes](DEVELOPMENT.md) for previous versions. Historical test results are not a current guarantee.

## v1.34: adaptive engine and device benchmark

AUTO STUDIO is optional. It samples the unprocessed input with a native 2048-point analyser every 250 ms, estimates six spectral bands, and gradually adjusts four existing EQ bands. Corrections are bounded between -2.5 and +2 dB depending on the band, with -4 dB headroom. It is a lightweight heuristic, not machine learning or source separation. Analysis disconnects on pause, buffering, hidden tabs and other EQ selections; the previous correction is held when analysis is paused. Track changes and seeking reset the correction.

Calibration used four privately supplied tracks: 2,358 offline spectral windows and 16 isolated Chromium OfflineAudioContext renders of eight-second excerpts (eight baseline and eight adaptive). The isolated adaptive renders included -4 dB headroom; none exceeded full scale, compared with 56 above-full-scale samples in the unprocessed references. This is not a level-matched sound-quality comparison, a full player chain test, or a physical-device performance measurement. Maximum observed analyser/controller call time in that offline experiment was 0.5 ms. No audio or training data is distributed.

The new TEST PERF button runs a silent synthetic benchmark only with playback paused or stopped. It measures two-second main-thread Q16/remix processing and isolated native offline EQ/convolution renders, including impulse construction time. Export the diagnostic JSON afterward. These timings are not real-time CPU utilization, underrun counts or end-to-end playback latency. No audio is played, uploaded or downloaded by the benchmark.

Validation of the integrated code: JavaScript syntax, 1,002 adaptive controller checks and 11 mocked analyser lifecycle checks. CSS, Q16/remix core, bass profiles and reverb implementation match v1.33 exactly. The complete player and benchmark have not been retested on physical ChromeOS or in a real browser in this version.

## Runtime, privacy and limitations

AudioWorklet is preferred. The fallback uses a ScriptProcessor buffer of 8192 frames for resampling/remix; fallback timing may differ. The app uses the system audio output, and headphone disconnection can switch sound to speakers. Start at a moderate volume, especially when using boost or headphones.

No telemetry, upload, external fonts, bundled music, model weights or network requests in the standalone player. Files remain local; settings are stored in the browser when allowed. Reopen the folder after closing the browser. Diagnostic reports are exported manually. The README badges are hosted by Shields.io and are not dependencies of the HTML player.

## 1.43 Studio Room

STUDIO ROOM reproduces the exact LIBRE reverb settings selected by Shield-77: 0.30 s duration, NATURAL tone, 0 ms pre-delay, 100% wet mix. It shares the same impulse generation and cache key as these LIBRE settings. The preset does not overwrite custom LIBRE preferences, bass profiles, EQ, pitch or volume. LONG is disabled for this fixed room. For the original listening combination, select DEEP + PUNCH and POP ROCK STUDIO independently. This is a synthetic room, not an acoustic measurement of a physical studio.

Validation: exact room parameter equality and 112,860 identical finite impulse samples across 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz; JavaScript syntax and 15 recovery checks passed. Shield-77 subsequently confirmed by listening on their Chromebook that STUDIO ROOM reproduces the desired room sound. This is a subjective listening confirmation, not a measured physical acoustic or latency test.

## 1.42 Beat Sync

SHAKE now uses up to 60 visual updates per second, a 1024-point unsmoothed analyser at 44.1/48 kHz (2048 at higher rates), and a two-frame onset comparison with a 6 dB rise and 7 dB excess threshold. The 160 ms retrigger guard and 18% maximum zoom remain. SPECTRUM retains its 2048-point smoothed analyser and approximately 30 fps updates; VINYL and the audio graph are unchanged.

Validation: Chromium OfflineAudioContext rendered the user's 115.278 s live reference through the exact native bass profiles, compressor and fixed ROCK STUDIO baseline curve at nominal 25% volume. Offline Blackman-window DFT sampling simulated the previous and new detector at 30 and 60 Hz. All four bass profiles, no effects, static ROCK baseline and combined maximum bass + static ROCK were compared.

| Configuration | Previous triggers | New triggers |
|---|---:|---:|
| No effects | 341 | 347 |
| PUNCH | 346 | 350 |
| DEEP BASS | 327 | 332 |
| ROCK DRIVE | 347 | 354 |
| DEEP + PUNCH | 330 | 331 |
| ROCK baseline | 342 | 351 |
| DEEP + PUNCH + ROCK baseline | 331 | 334 |

Ten synthetic bass pulses were all detected in three configurations; simulated detection time was 43 ms before and 21 ms after, including native compressor delay in the offline graph. This is measured relative to synthetic source onset at the tested frame phase, not physical audio/visual latency. Live trigger counts are not annotated kick counts. Adaptive ROCK corrections, reverb, Glitch Lab, real-time UI timing and physical device latency were not included in this rendering test. 32 mocked visual checks and 15 recovery checks passed. No source audio distributed.

## 1.41 Live Impact

SHAKE uses a 160 ms minimum onset interval, a stronger relative bass-rise threshold and a 90 ms exponential decay. An offline 30 Hz FFT simulation on a user-supplied 115.3 s live recording, at nominal 25% volume and no added effects, yielded 336 triggers instead of 448 and reduced time above 2% zoom from 72.9% to 50.5%. These are algorithm trigger counts, not annotated musical beat counts or actual ChromeOS rendering measurements. Maximum zoom remains 18%. No audio or cover from the recording is distributed. All 28 mocked visual tests passed; the actual playback and display still need device verification.

## 1.40 Big Vinyl

VINYL fills 98% of the smaller available stage dimension instead of 88%; album art occupies 78% of the record diameter instead of 66%. The fallback logo is also enlarged without stretching. The nominal speed is now 10 rpm (one revolution every six seconds at original playback speed), still proportional to pitch. An AGRANDIR button opens a larger record view; REDUIRE or Escape restores the normal layout. The visualizer, SHAKE and audio engine are unchanged. 26 simulated visual tests passed; the actual ChromeOS layout remains to be verified.

## 1.39 Bass Impact

SHAKE now follows real 35–160 Hz bass onsets using a rolling dB reference, a short refractory period and a damped rebound. Each hit expands the artwork by up to 18% and adds bounded, alternating movement, with margins to keep the image visible. Sustained bass settles instead of producing constant artificial motion. No flashes, no change to the audio path; the existing reduced-motion and STATIC settings remain available. 22 simulated visual/parser tests pass, including loud and quieter onsets, damping, silence and mode switching. Perceived synchronization and appearance still require physical-device testing.

## 1.38 Visual Studio

The spare space in the effects panel now contains local cover art and four display modes: SPECTRUM (40 logarithmic bands from a native FFT after the effects and volume), SHAKE (bounded movement on bass transients), VINYL (rotating record with cover in its label, speed linked to playback rate) and STATIC (no animation or analysis). In v1.38, visual updates were capped at approximately 30 fps; v1.42 raises the SHAKE cap to 60 fps. Animation and the analyser connection stop when paused, hidden, static, stopped or reduced-motion is requested; vinyl requires no analyser.

Artwork is read only for the selected track. Supported embedded images are MP3 ID3 APIC/PIC, FLAC PICTURE and Ogg Vorbis/Opus METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE. Local JPEG, PNG or WebP sidecar images may also be imported alongside audio: same stem, cover, folder, front or album in the same folder. Unsupported or absent artwork falls back to the supplied SHIELD DJ Lite logo, embedded as a 2.9 KB WebP, fitted without stretching. The original source image remains unmodified; no web requests, online album lookup or third-party metadata library. Reads are capped at 4 MiB; images larger than 16 megapixels are rejected. The current artwork URL is released when tracks change. M4A embedded artwork is not yet supported; sidecars still work.

16 mocked parser and visual lifecycle checks pass. The audio DSP and graph initialization are unchanged. Real browser layout, perceived synchronization and RAM/CPU use require device testing.

## 1.37 Rock & Free Room

ROCK STUDIO now uses the existing native analyser and four bounded corrections on top of a gentler seven-band curve. Offline calibration used 190 complete five-second windows across four reference recordings (Wet Floor compilation, Sea Me Now, Triple Dip, Clickbait), with stereo mean Welch spectra at 24 kHz. No recordings, models, or training assets are distributed. These are heuristic settings, not a trained model or source separation. Compression is gentler unless other heavy effects are enabled.

LIBRE offers independent 0–100% equal-power mix, seven durations from 0.30 to 5.00 s, three tone choices and five pre-delays from 0 to 100 ms. Mix changes reuse the existing impulse; other settings rebuild it on selection. Cached impulses remain subject to the 3 MiB budget. At 100% mix the direct path is silent. Earlier saved LIBRE percentages now represent the actual mix, rather than a 65% maximum.

JavaScript syntax, 15 calibration/room/structure checks and 15 simulated recovery checks passed. Browser layout, real playback, listening quality and RAM consumption still require device verification.

## 1.36 streamlined

Removed the Digital Crush effect, its controls and its separate audio processor. RESET FX, all Glitch Lab effects and the resampling engine remain. Pitch buttons and arrows now change speed by 0.025x, while the slider keeps its 0.001x resolution. Syntax, 10 pitch/structure checks and 15 simulated recovery checks passed; physical-device playback has not yet been retested.

## 1.35 stability maintenance

No new audio effects or EQ curves: this update focuses on the existing audio graph.

- AudioWorklet processor failures switch to the native/fallback audio path instead of leaving a failed processor in the graph.
- The 8192-frame fallback keeps the original signal audible until two processed buffers have arrived, and schedules the transition using the audio playback clock. When disabled, it fades out before disconnecting.
- Fallback processing exceptions restore the original signal and record the error in the diagnostic report. Reverb setup failures also restore the direct signal.
- Reverb disposal is idempotent and tolerates cleanup errors.

Validation for 1.35: JavaScript syntax checked; 15 simulated audio-graph recovery/cleanup assertions, 63 synthetic DSP scenarios and 15 resampling checks passed. The graph tests use test doubles, not an actual AudioContext. Real Chromium playback, sustained playback and testing this specific version on the target Chromebook are still required. ScriptProcessor remains a main-thread fallback and cannot guarantee gap-free playback under load.

## Français

**Lecteur audio et studio de remix gratuit, libre et entièrement local**, conçu en priorité pour les Chromebook ASUS CM14. L'interface classique est conservée. Le moteur s'inspire de Shield DJ Lite et de Shield Theme Maker, avec une adaptation aux API natives de Chrome.

[Télécharger le ZIP](https://github.com/Shield-77/Shield-DJ-Lite-Web/archive/refs/heads/main.zip), extraire `index.html`, l'ouvrir dans Chrome et importer ses fichiers. Pas d'installation ni de connexion requise pour écouter. Les boutons −/+ et les flèches avancent de 0,025× ; le curseur tactile ou souris garde une résolution de 0,001×. Crush / Digital Remix a été retiré, mais RESET FX et le Glitch Lab sont conservés. Les effets audio, les profils de basses et la réverbération restent disponibles.

Je possède moi-même le Chromebook cible et j'ai testé le lecteur sur cet appareil (versions précédentes). Je choisis les fonctionnalités et réalise les essais ; ChatGPT m'aide à développer le port Web, tandis que Codex a participé aux projets 3DS d'origine. Le projet est conçu pour partager, pas pour imposer un abonnement.
